Use calendar weeks consistently in the extension’s configured timezone, exclude incomplete future weeks, and keep installation identifiers inside aggregation logic. Acceptance: the table shows cohort size and retention percentages, small cohorts do not produce divide-by-zero errors, fixture results are deterministic, and tests cover users active across week boundaries.

Build a global content delivery and publishing platform for video, documents, interactive packages, and accessibility metadata. Store immutable source assets in S3-compatible object storage, transcode media with queued workers, publish through a multi-CDN layer, and protect downloads with signed URLs, DRM-ready interfaces, and entitlement checks. Support versioned releases, regional failover, cache invalidation, malware scanning, and legal holds. Acceptance requires resumable uploads, integrity verification, WCAG metadata preservation, tenant isolation, upload-to-publish observability, and tested recovery of a complete course catalog.

Modernize the legacy math notebook into a React and TypeScript SPA while keeping existing URLs, notebooks, and kernel protocols working through a compatibility layer. Add typed executable cells, LaTeX and Markdown, symbolic and numeric outputs, dependency-aware reruns, rich error locations, collaborative editing, comments, version history, and offline drafts. Isolate execution in sandboxed workers or containers and support reconnects to remote kernels. Acceptance requires zero-loss migration, deterministic replay, kernel failure recovery, large-notebook performance, screen-reader coverage, extension APIs, and end-to-end tests for representative legacy notebooks.

Refactor the Python/PySide6 desktop machine-learning workbench’s background execution into a durable local job platform. Separate scheduling, workers, artifact storage, and UI observation; support process isolation, GPU and CPU resource quotas, resumable checkpoints, cancellation, retries, and optional remote workers over authenticated gRPC. Preserve existing project manifests and result formats. Acceptance: queued jobs survive app restarts, failed workers do not corrupt artifacts, concurrent workloads respect quotas, old projects run unchanged, and integration tests cover crash recovery, version skew, and offline operation.

Add a PrometheusRule for node filesystem pressure in the production cluster. Fire when available space on non-temporary filesystems is below 10% for 15 minutes, label it severity=critical and team=platform, and include the existing runbook URL annotation. Use the current Alertmanager route and do not alert on pseudo-filesystems or read-only mounts. Acceptance: promtool rule validation passes, the expression excludes those mounts, and the alert appears in the rendered monitoring manifest.

Update release notes for version 3.2 of the Node.js `shipit` CLI. Summarize the new `rollback --to`, changed default timeout, deprecated `--legacy-auth`, and any migration action users must take. Edit `CHANGELOG.md` and the upgrade guide only; follow the repository's Keep a Changelog headings and link style. Separate user-visible behavior from internal fixes, and do not invent issue numbers. Acceptance: the notes are understandable without commit history and every command or option name matches the shipped `--help` output.

In the Elixir/Phoenix app, find the CSRF boundary in `lib/my_app_web/plugs/browser_security.ex`. Research which browser routes receive the plug, how JSON requests are classified, and whether an origin or token check can be bypassed through content-type variation. Use the existing endpoint pipeline and tests; do not change router structure. Acceptance: list the affected route class, give a minimal reproducible request if a gap exists, and recommend the smallest plug-local change or state that coverage is sufficient.

Migrate the existing browser extension from Manifest V2 to Manifest V3 without breaking page integrations. Replace background pages with a service-worker architecture, redesign content-script injection and long-lived messaging, move blocking rules to declarativeNetRequest where possible, and handle CSP, host permissions, downloads, and Firefox compatibility. Keep TypeScript APIs stable for existing features and provide telemetry plus a rollback flag. Acceptance requires Chrome and Firefox production builds, no lost events during worker suspension, equivalent allow and block behavior, regression coverage for major sites, bundle-size budgets, and a documented phased release plan.

Fix care-team authorization leaks in the Ruby on Rails API and React administration console. Model organization, facility, specialty, patient assignment, break-glass access, delegation, and expiration consistently across read, write, search, export, and background-job paths. Invalidate permission caches when memberships or assignments change, preserve least privilege for service accounts, and produce auditable break-glass events without exposing sensitive reasons. Acceptance criteria: unauthorized records are inaccessible through every endpoint and UI route, legitimate cross-facility coverage works, revoked access takes effect promptly, emergency access requires justification, and automated security tests cover tenant, role, and cache-invalidation combinations.

Fix the enrollment search query in app/Models/Enrollment.php. Keep pagination, authorization checks, case-insensitive search, and the existing archived-enrollment behavior. Group the name predicates under the school constraint without changing the public scope signature. Acceptance: results never cross school boundaries, matching names remain searchable, and unfiltered results are unchanged.

In the Node.js CLI, add a `devtools lighthouse-report <file>` command that reads a Lighthouse JSON report and prints a compact table for performance, accessibility, best practices, and SEO. Support stdin via `-` and return a clear error for invalid JSON or missing categories. Add parser tests, CLI snapshot tests, and help text. Acceptance: output is deterministic, threshold defaults are documented, and existing commands are unaffected.

Fix homework attachment downloads in server/storage/signed_url.ts. Files with spaces or non-ASCII names currently receive malformed S3 signed URLs because the object key is encoded twice. Acceptance: the generated URL fetches the intended object and ordinary filenames remain compatible.

In the existing TypeScript Chrome Manifest V3 extension, add an options-page usage analytics view backed by the extension’s local event store. Aggregate daily counts for popup opens, content-script actions, and completed tasks over selectable 7, 30, and 90-day ranges; exclude raw URLs and user text. Add a lightweight table, sparkline-style CSS bars, and loading and empty states. Acceptance: aggregates match fixture data, date filters update without reload, sensitive fields never render, and unit tests cover timezone boundaries and no-event cases.

In the existing Vue 3 + TypeScript operations dashboard, modify only `src/components/QueueControls.vue`. Add Pause and Resume buttons for an automation queue, showing exactly one based on the `paused` prop, plus a disabled Clear button when `pendingCount` is zero. Emit `pause`, `resume`, and `clear` without changing public prop names or adding dependencies. Use the project’s existing button classes and accessible labels. Acceptance: emitted events fire once, disabled state is correct, controls work with keyboard focus, and current typecheck/lint commands remain clean.

Rotate the browser extension's CI credentials without changing runtime behavior. Replace the existing Chrome Web Store, Firefox AMO, and Sentry tokens with newly named GitHub Actions secrets, update all workflow references, remove legacy variable names and local secret examples, and document the required secret names in the repository README. Keep secrets masked and out of generated bundles. Acceptance: a release dry run succeeds with the new names, secret scanning finds no values, and old names are unused.

Configure Prometheus Alertmanager routing for the existing Kubernetes services. Add a route for alerts labeled team=platform and severity=critical to the PagerDuty receiver, while retaining the default Slack route for warning alerts. Keep grouping by alertname and namespace, set a five-minute repeat interval for critical alerts, and avoid duplicate notifications through inhibition rules. Develop a distributed resilience and test harness for the checkout platform, using Java services, Kubernetes, Temporal workflows, Kafka, PostgreSQL, and Stripe sandbox integrations. Cover retries, idempotency, payment authorization, inventory reservation, fraud holds, partial outages, duplicate webhooks, and recovery after region loss. Add deterministic fault injection, contract tests, end-to-end browser scenarios, soak tests, and trace correlation. Acceptance requires repeatable chaos experiments in CI and staging, no double charges or orders under injected failures, bounded recovery-time measurements, and actionable artifacts for every failed scenario.

Build automated rotation for AWS IAM and database credentials used by services, CI, and scheduled jobs. Use IAM roles and STS wherever possible, AWS Secrets Manager for unavoidable secrets, and a Lambda or Step Functions workflow for staged rotation with overlap and rollback. Inventory current consumers, update SDK configuration and Kubernetes integrations, alert on failed or overdue rotations, and remove obsolete keys only after health checks succeed. Acceptance: all in-scope credentials have owners and rotation intervals, production rotation completes without downtime, revoked credentials are rejected, failures page the on-call team, and an auditable report proves no static key remains in the repository.

Build a batch and online recommendation subsystem for the marketplace using Python, Kafka, Feast, and a PostgreSQL-backed catalog. Implement event ingestion, feature definitions, offline training, candidate generation, ranking, cold-start fallbacks, diversity constraints, and an authenticated low-latency API. Track model and feature versions, prevent future-data leakage in training, and add Airflow orchestration plus offline metrics such as NDCG, recall, coverage, and calibration. Acceptance: reproducible training from fixtures, p95 API latency under 100 ms, safe behavior for new users and items, monitored freshness, and contract and integration tests for event schema evolution.

Create a governed security telemetry platform that collects high-volume logs and traces from Kubernetes, cloud accounts, hosts, identity providers, and CI/CD. Use OpenTelemetry collectors, Kafka, ClickHouse or OpenSearch, and object storage with tenant-aware RBAC and immutable retention tiers. Define redaction and data-minimization rules, schema evolution, clock handling, sampling, detection feeds, and disaster recovery. Acceptance: ingestion scales through peak load, sensitive fields are demonstrably removed, queries meet analyst latency targets, retention and deletion policies are enforced, and replayed incidents reproduce expected timelines.

Write a troubleshooting guide for the Java Click-based `harbor` CLI, focusing on login failures, expired tokens, missing profiles, permission errors, and nonzero exits in CI. Add `docs/troubleshooting.md` and link it from the README. For each symptom, provide the diagnostic command, likely cause, safe remediation, and escalation clue; never tell users to print secrets. Keep examples POSIX-shell compatible. Acceptance: a clean user can follow the guide, all commands exist in `harbor --help`, and security-sensitive values are redacted.

Audit the Zephyr Bluetooth Mesh implementation on nRF52 nodes and the companion Kotlin provisioning tool. Review provisioning, friendship and low-power nodes, relay selection, subscription management, key refresh, rejoin behavior, message segmentation, replay protection, and firmware-version compatibility. Trace failures caused by packet loss, sleeping relays, duplicate addresses, and network partition healing. Check whether mobile-side retries can create unsafe or inconsistent device state. Acceptance requires a ranked cross-platform review with protocol evidence, security and battery implications, reproducible edge cases, and a test matrix covering multi-hop and recovery scenarios.

Add a required GitHub Actions policy job for the Manifest V3 browser extension. Build the production bundle with pnpm and inspect the generated manifest for an approved permission and host-permission allowlist, reject unexpected debug flags, and fail when either Chrome or Firefox ZIP exceeds 5 MB. Keep the checks deterministic and expose violations in the job summary. Acceptance: branch protection can require the job, a newly added permission fails with an actionable message, and valid bundles pass on Linux runners.

In the React storefront and Symfony/PHP order API, fix split-shipment summaries charging the customer’s shipping fee once per package instead of applying the existing combined-order rule. Calculate shipping from the shipment group totals, preserve free-shipping thresholds and promotion exclusions, and return one authoritative amount for both checkout and the confirmation page. Do not change carrier rate selection. Add API and UI regression tests for one, two, and mixed-rate shipments; acceptance is matching totals with no duplicate shipping charge.

Harden the EKS platform against common workload and supply-chain risks using Pod Security Admission, Kyverno, NetworkPolicy, strict RBAC, IRSA, private endpoints, and Cosign image-signature verification. Inventory current exceptions, separate enforcement by environment, and provide a controlled process for temporary waivers with expiry and ownership. Update base images, admission policies, CI checks, and operational documentation. Acceptance requires policy unit tests, a CIS-aligned assessment, successful deployment of existing services, blocked negative test cases, actionable audit logs, and a tested emergency rollback path.

Fix destructive workspace cleanup in the Rust CLI and its distributed workspace service. Cleanup currently misidentifies shared mounts, reused persistent volumes, interrupted jobs, and workspaces with active leases, occasionally deleting user data. Preserve the existing workspace layout and command interface while adding ownership identities, lease fencing, quarantine-before-delete behavior, crash recovery, and an auditable dry-run mode. Acceptance requires filesystem and Kubernetes integration tests, simulated clock and crash tests, protection against symlink and traversal attacks, safe operation across multiple controllers, and zero deletion of active or externally owned data.

Replace the host-level nightly shell cron with a Kubernetes CronJob managed by the existing Helm chart. Run the current container command at 02:00 UTC, set concurrencyPolicy to Forbid, backoffLimit to 2, and activeDeadlineSeconds to 900, and retain current ConfigMap and Secret references. Make schedule and suspend configurable but default them to the existing behavior. Acceptance: helm lint and template pass, only one run can execute at once, and failed jobs are retried within the deadline.

In the Expo React Native TypeScript finance app, add an amortization schedule for a fixed-rate loan. Calculate the monthly payment and remaining balance using cents-safe arithmetic, show principal and interest per month, and support zero-interest loans plus optional monthly overpayments. Stop at a final shortened payment rather than producing a negative balance. Add a collapsible schedule section, Jest tests against a known 30-year example, and cases for zero rate and overpayment. Acceptance: the schedule's payments reconcile to the requested principal and the final balance is exactly zero.

In the C++/Qt desktop app, refactor `DocumentTabs::findById` in `src/DocumentTabs.cpp`. The current function scans the tab list in multiple branches and repeats comparison logic for pinned and normal tabs. Consolidate the lookup into one readable path, preserving ID case sensitivity, pinned-tab precedence, and the existing null result when no tab matches. Do not change the container type or header API. Acceptance: current C++ tests pass for pinned, duplicate, missing, and empty IDs, and the edit remains confined to this implementation file.

In `src/hooks/useProjects.ts` for the React/TypeScript SPA, expose a typed error state when the existing projects request fails and clear it when a later request succeeds. Keep the current data and loading APIs compatible, do not log or swallow errors, and distinguish an abort or unmount from a real request failure. The consuming screen already renders an `ErrorBanner`; pass it the existing error message without adding a new component. Acceptance: failed requests show the banner, successful retries remove it, and stale errors do not reappear.

In the Node/TypeScript file `src/automation/next-run.ts`, implement `nextRunAfter(lastRun, intervalMinutes, now)` for a polling bot. Return the earliest UTC timestamp strictly after `lastRun` that is greater than or equal to `now`, using fixed intervals rather than repeated-call drift. For `intervalMinutes <= 0`, throw a typed error. Preserve millisecond precision and avoid local-time or DST behavior. Acceptance checks cover times before, between, and exactly on run boundaries, plus a long gap requiring several skipped intervals.

Build an equation-transformation lab across a React/TypeScript canvas, a Go API, and a symbolic-math worker. Students must manipulate both sides of equations, preserve equivalence, inspect operation history, and receive feedback that distinguishes legal transformations from accidental answer matching. Support linear, quadratic, rational, and unit-bearing equations with configurable curriculum limits. Acceptance includes a canonical expression model, server-side validation, undo and replay, accessibility for keyboard-only use, latency measurements, teacher-configurable policies, and regression tests for edge cases such as zero denominators and extraneous roots.

Launch a secure remote-diagnostics platform for embedded products with lightweight C agents and a Go control plane. Provide consented log collection, metrics, crash dumps, traces, bounded remote commands, packet captures, and support bundles over low-bandwidth links without interactive shell access. Include end-to-end encryption, role-based access, redaction, retention, rate limits, audit trails, tenant isolation, offline queuing, and battery-aware scheduling. Acceptance requires a threat model, device resource budgets, APIs, operator workflows, forensic integrity checks, fault-injection and soak tests, staged rollout, and SLOs for retrieving diagnostics from 99% of reachable devices.

In the TypeScript file `src/agent/token_budget.ts`, implement `remainingBudget(limit, used, reserve)` for a bot that must preserve a response reserve. Return `max(0, limit - used - reserve)` as an integer. Reject non-finite or negative arguments and throw unless all three values are safe integers; do not silently round fractional inputs. The helper must not call a tokenizer or alter state. Acceptance checks cover zero, exact exhaustion, over-budget usage, a reserve larger than the limit, and invalid numeric values.

Produce a phased architecture and implementation plan for a multi-tenant fleet OTA platform serving STM32 and ESP32 devices. Use Rust services, C firmware, PostgreSQL, S3-compatible object storage, and MQTT over cellular links. Cover signed full and delta images, secure-boot integration, hardware compatibility gates, staged rings, resumable downloads, power-loss recovery, rollback, auditability, tenant isolation, and 100,000-device scale. The plan is accepted only if it includes API and data models, threat model, migration sequencing, load and fault tests, observability, runbooks, staffing estimates, and measurable pilot exit criteria.

Review the Go aggregation function that builds network-waterfall bars from DevTools request timing phases. Check missing phases, negative or overlapping intervals, redirects, cached requests, and clock-unit conversion. Ensure the output remains deterministic and never emits NaN or negative widths, while preserving valid timing data. Acceptance: identify specific bugs or omissions with examples and line references; keep the review to this function and do not change the API.

For the Python Click CLI, add parametrized tests for the report command’s format flags. Cover the default table output, JSON and CSV formats, the short alias, an unknown format, and combining --quiet with a valid format. Use in-memory fixtures and capsys; avoid filesystem, network, and locale dependence. Acceptance: pytest passes, each valid mode has a stable representative assertion, invalid input returns the documented nonzero code, and quiet mode suppresses progress output without changing report data.

Refactor the multi-tenant Django/React platform so tenant isolation is enforced consistently at API, database, cache, object-storage, background-job, and analytics boundaries. Introduce typed authorization policies and PostgreSQL row-level security behind a compatibility layer, preserving existing roles and district-specific permissions. Audit every cross-tenant query, migrate legacy records safely, and keep operational support access explicitly scoped and logged. Acceptance: automated negative tests prove no tenant leakage, authorized workflows remain behaviorally compatible, performance stays within 10 percent of baseline, migrations are reversible, and security review signs off before enforcement is enabled.

Build a multi-tenant virtual classroom frontend in Next.js and TypeScript that combines WebRTC video, live chat, collaborative whiteboard, breakout rooms, polls, attendance, captions, and teacher moderation. Integrate existing media, identity, and notification services through typed clients, with graceful degradation for low bandwidth and mobile browsers. Support session recording controls, timezone-aware scheduling, keyboard navigation, localization, and WCAG 2.2 AA. Acceptance: 500-participant load scenarios remain usable, reconnects preserve classroom state, captions and moderation events are auditable, critical flows have Playwright coverage, and rollout supports tenant-level feature flags.

In the SvelteKit/TypeScript product page, fix the recommendation widget showing unavailable variants as purchasable after inventory changes. Filter variants using the same availability data as the add-to-cart path, refresh that data when the widget loads, and remove only unavailable choices without hiding an otherwise available product. Preserve selected options when still valid and show the existing sold-out treatment otherwise. Add component tests for mixed inventory and an all-unavailable response; acceptance is no disabled-stock variant can be added to cart.

In our Python/FastAPI service, update Alembic's env.py to make migrations use the DATABASE_URL connection while preserving offline generation. Read the URL from existing settings, avoid opening a second engine, and keep current PostgreSQL schema naming and transaction behavior. Do not alter migration files or application models. Acceptance: `alembic upgrade head` uses the configured URL in online mode, `alembic upgrade head --sql` still emits SQL without connecting, and existing migration tests pass.

Rework the location-browsing experience in the Flutter app using the existing Mapbox integration. Provide clustered markers, current-location permission states, a synchronized map/list layout, draggable detail sheets, category and distance filters, saved places, search-to-location behavior, and loading, offline, and error states. Keep map gestures responsive, avoid unnecessary marker rebuilds, respect safe areas and orientation changes, and preserve existing place APIs. Acceptance: selecting a marker and selecting a list item stay synchronized, clusters expand predictably, permissions can be retried, filters survive navigation, saved changes update immediately, and widget tests cover the major interaction and failure paths.

Implement a signed-release system for application binaries, container images, Helm charts, and Terraform modules. Use Sigstore Cosign with keyless or KMS-backed signing, generate SLSA-compatible provenance in GitHub Actions, publish attestations alongside artifacts, and define verification libraries and CLI checks for deployment and consumption. Protect signing permissions with isolated environments and approvals, support key or certificate rotation, and preserve verification during rollback. Acceptance: each production artifact maps to an approved commit and workflow identity, unsigned or tampered artifacts are rejected by release gates, downstream Kubernetes and package consumers verify signatures, provenance is queryable, and a documented emergency recovery path does not permit silent bypasses.

In `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, switch the deployment job from the retired `DATABASE_PASSWORD` repository secret to `DATABASE_PASSWORD_V2`, while keeping the username, host, and staging/production environment mapping unchanged. Pass the password only through the existing process environment; do not echo it, write it to artifacts, or change application code. Acceptance: the YAML parses, every database migration and deploy step receives the new secret, no reference to the retired secret remains in the workflow, and the existing PostgreSQL connection format is preserved.

Create a multi-cluster Kubernetes security admission platform using Gatekeeper/OPA, Kyverno where appropriate, and policy bundles distributed through Argo CD. Cover privileged containers, host mounts, image provenance, resource limits, network policy, namespace tenancy, and Pod Security Standards, with warn-to-enforce rollout and explicit emergency exemptions. Include Rego tests, signed versioned bundles, policy observability, developer feedback, and upgrade compatibility for EKS and GKE. Acceptance: policy decisions are auditable, bypasses expire automatically, CI blocks violations, and all clusters converge from Git.

In the Electron TypeScript memory panel, add a retained-size delta column to heap snapshot comparison results. Compute the delta from the baseline snapshot, format bytes using the panel’s existing units, support ascending and descending sort, and render an em dash when an object exists in only one snapshot. Keep parsing off the UI thread through the current worker interface and preserve existing columns. Add comparison and formatting unit tests plus a fixture with added and removed nodes. Acceptance: sorting is stable, large snapshots do not freeze the panel, and current snapshot loading behavior is unchanged.

Fix route flapping and forwarding loops in a 6LoWPAN/Thread mesh running Zephyr on sleepy 802.15.4 nodes with a Rust border-router service. The repair must handle parent churn, partition healing, duplicated advertisements, low-power polling, channel changes, and border-router failover without exhausting battery or neighbor tables. Preserve IPv6 interoperability and existing security credentials. Add a deterministic network simulator, radio-fault injection, topology telemetry, and multi-border convergence tests. Acceptance: a 500-node, 30-day accelerated soak maintains bounded reconvergence, no persistent loops or black holes, and meets packet-delivery and sleep-current budgets under specified loss rates.

In the React Native TypeScript health app, improve the small line-chart axis component by generating human-readable numeric ticks. Implement a deterministic 1/2/5 × 10^n step selection, include zero when the range crosses it, cap labels at six, and handle equal, negative, and very small ranges. Keep chart layout unchanged and format labels without scientific notation for ordinary values. Add unit tests for each range class and snapshot the existing screen. Acceptance: ticks are monotonic, cover the data range, and never overlap the plotted bounds.

Fix background location tracking in the native iOS and Android field-service app, where frequent GPS polling drains batteries, misses geofences, and continues after logout. Rework lifecycle ownership, permission upgrades, significant-change and fused-location strategies, batching, accuracy thresholds, and server upload scheduling. Respect platform background limits, approximate-location choices, privacy disclosures, and tenant-specific tracking policies. Add instrumentation for sampling rate and battery impact, plus simulated-route tests for killed, suspended, offline, and permission-denied states. Acceptance: trips remain accurate enough for dispatch, tracking stops promptly when required, and measured idle battery use meets the agreed budget.

Fix the Room and SQLite migration path in the Android/Kotlin app after upgrading from schema versions 12 through 16. Some users lose drafts or crash on startup because migrations assume complete rows, run twice, or leave indexes inconsistent after an interrupted upgrade. Define a forward-only migration strategy, backfill nullable fields safely, preserve encrypted records, and provide a recoverable backup and rollback boundary without silently deleting user data. Test every supported version jump, low-storage interruption, process death, and downgrade refusal. Acceptance: existing drafts and sync metadata survive all upgrades, startup never loops, and failures produce actionable diagnostics.

Review the TypeScript worker that consumes SQS messages and retries failed enrichment calls. Ensure transient HTTP 429 and 5xx errors use the existing visibility-timeout policy, while permanent 4xx errors are sent to the dead-letter queue with structured context. Keep message schema and concurrency limits unchanged. Acceptance: tests cover retry, dead-letter, and successful acknowledgement paths; no message is acknowledged before persistence; lint and the targeted test suite pass.

Build a complete checkout flow in the Flutter mobile app using Dart, Riverpod, and the existing REST client. Create cart review, address selection/editing, delivery option, payment via the existing Stripe PaymentSheet wrapper, order review, success, and recoverable failure screens. Persist form state across navigation, validate fields inline, handle loading, retry, and idempotent submission, respect keyboard and safe-area insets, and support Android/iOS back behavior. Acceptance: users can complete a happy-path order, recover from expired payment or network errors without duplicate orders, accessibility labels exist, and widget tests cover each state.

Develop an architecture and phased delivery plan for a digital-twin service representing device identity, desired state, reported state, topology, firmware, and time-series health. Use TypeScript APIs, Go or Rust workers, PostgreSQL for authoritative state, an event bus, and a time-series store. Support eventual consistency, offline devices, out-of-order events, schema versioning, command idempotency, tenant isolation, and replayable history. Acceptance requires state-transition semantics, conflict resolution, API contracts, retention policy, scale estimates for ten million twins, simulator coverage, disaster recovery, and migration from shadow state already stored in devices.

Fix corruption in the distributed content-addressed cache used by our Go CLI and remote build workers. The cache combines local filesystem layers, an S3-compatible object store, Redis locks, and concurrent garbage collection. Preserve cache keys and existing artifacts while making writes atomic, validating checksums, handling interrupted uploads, and preventing deletion of live entries across regions. Add repair and verification commands plus failure-injection coverage. Acceptance: no corrupted artifact after 1,000 concurrent writers, safe recovery from process and network crashes, bounded lock contention, and backward-compatible reads of all supported cache generations.

Create a finance reconciliation service comparing PostgreSQL ledger facts with BigQuery sales and payment aggregates. Define a versioned reconciliation contract for time zones, currencies, fees, refunds, and settlement timing; load source snapshots, match at transaction and daily levels, classify tolerances, and persist immutable discrepancy cases. Provide reruns, evidence attachments, approvals, and exportable audit reports. Acceptance requires balanced control totals, deterministic results, late-arriving correction handling, access controls, performance on a year of data, integration tests, and an operator runbook.

Add the missing `calculate_fee` function in the existing Python FastAPI billing module. For card payments, charge 2.9% plus $0.30; for ACH, charge 0.8% capped at $5.00. Accept a positive `Decimal` amount and return the fee in cents rounded with `ROUND_HALF_UP`; reject zero or negative amounts and unknown methods with the module’s existing validation exception. Keep currency fixed to USD and do not alter the endpoint schema. Acceptance covers both formulas, the ACH cap, and cent-boundary rounding.

Implement an adaptive algebra mastery-path subsystem in our Python FastAPI and React/TypeScript learning platform. Combine Bayesian knowledge tracing with item difficulty estimates, prerequisite graphs, spaced review, and teacher overrides; explain every recommendation and avoid repeating inaccessible skills. Persist versioned learner state in PostgreSQL, process events idempotently, and expose batch and realtime recommendations with privacy-safe analytics. Acceptance criteria: recommendations are reproducible from an event snapshot, cold-start and missing-data behavior is documented, dashboards show mastery changes, migration scripts are reversible, and simulation tests demonstrate improved coverage without violating prerequisite ordering.

In the existing Rust import crate, add unit tests for the transaction CSV parser in one module. Cover quoted commas in merchant names, a UTF-8 currency symbol, a missing optional memo, and a malformed amount; assert the parsed cents, optional field, and error variant rather than matching unstable text. Keep fixtures inline, avoid filesystem or network dependencies, and do not change parser behavior. Acceptance: `cargo test` passes and the cases protect the current schema and validation rules.

Update the single options-page validation function in the existing TypeScript browser extension. It receives a comma-separated string of CSS selectors, trims whitespace, removes empty entries, and returns field-level errors for invalid selectors using `document.querySelector`, without throwing. Preserve the original selector text for valid entries and keep duplicate selectors in their original order. Do not change the settings schema or UI components. Acceptance: blank input is accepted as an empty list, malformed selectors produce a useful error, valid selectors are returned unchanged, and the options page remains responsive.

Add Enable/Disable behavior to the existing Manifest V3 extension popup using the already-present `#enabled-toggle` checkbox and only editing `src/popup.ts`. Use the existing `chrome.storage.sync` key `enabled`, defaulting to true when absent. Persist changes immediately and send the existing runtime message so content scripts apply the new state without a page reload. Preserve current popup styling and layout. Acceptance: opening the popup reflects stored state, toggling updates storage and message payload, and a disabled setting prevents the extension’s page action.

Implement universal links and Android app links for a React Native app with a Node.js API. Support password-reset, email-verification, invitation, and content-detail URLs; route cold starts, warm starts, and authenticated users correctly; preserve intended destinations through login; and reject expired or tampered tokens. Configure iOS associated domains, Android intent filters, staging and production hosts, and analytics attribution. Acceptance: links open the installed app or web fallback, navigation is deterministic after authentication, duplicate launches are harmless, and automated unit, integration, and real-device tests cover each lifecycle and environment.

Refactor data access in the React/TypeScript SPA from scattered fetch calls, useEffect lifecycles, and hand-written loading flags to TanStack Query with typed API clients. Cover list, detail, mutation, pagination, and dependent-query screens without changing backend contracts. Define query keys, stale-time defaults, invalidation rules, optimistic updates, cancellation, retry policy, and a consistent error boundary strategy. Preserve permissions and offline-friendly cached reads. Migrate the dashboard, projects, activity, and admin areas, then delete obsolete hooks and duplicated caches. Acceptance: no duplicate requests occur during navigation, mutations invalidate the right views, stale responses cannot overwrite newer data, and tests verify cache behavior and failure recovery.

Build a local search-insights table for the extension’s own search feature. From existing search events, show total searches, zero-result rate, and the ten most frequent normalized terms for the selected period. Trim whitespace, compare case-insensitively, and exclude empty queries; do not send terms to a server or expose them in logs. Acceptance: repeated searches are counted correctly, zero-result calculations use only completed searches, ties sort deterministically, the table has loading and empty states, and unit tests verify normalization, filtering, and date boundaries.

Ship a symbolic-calculus platform as a React and TypeScript SPA backed by a versioned computer-algebra service. The expression engine must represent canonical DAGs and support differentiation, integration, limits, series, equation solving, assumptions, simplification, units, and step-by-step explanations with proof metadata. Include a notebook, visual expression editor, collaborative projects, queued long-running jobs, deterministic caching, and LaTeX and MathML export. Acceptance requires agreement with a reference corpus, soundness checks for transformations, graceful timeouts, reproducible history, responsive large-expression editing, accessible output, API compatibility, and comprehensive property-based tests.

Build a production multi-model inference platform in Python and Go around Kubernetes and NVIDIA Triton. It must register versioned models, schedule GPU and CPU workloads across regions, support dynamic batching, autoscaling, streaming and synchronous APIs, tenant quotas, canary rollouts, and rollback. Persist metadata in PostgreSQL and artifacts in S3-compatible storage; expose OpenTelemetry metrics, traces, and audit logs. Provide Terraform, Helm, load tests, failure recovery, and documented security boundaries. Acceptance: deploys to a fresh cluster, passes contract and stress tests, meets defined p95 latency SLOs, and demonstrates zero-downtime model rollout.

Add a supported modding platform to an Unreal Engine 5 game using packaged content conventions and a sandboxed Lua scripting layer. Define a versioned manifest and dependency format, load-order and conflict rules, permission limits, save isolation, enable/disable flows, crash-safe recovery, and developer APIs for items, quests, and UI extensions. Provide local install and removal tooling plus hooks for a future workshop integration, without allowing arbitrary filesystem or network access. Acceptance: incompatible mods are rejected with actionable errors, a bad mod cannot corrupt base saves, deterministic multiplayer behavior is preserved, examples and API docs ship, and automated tests cover dependency cycles and rollback.

Map and review student-privacy risks across the monorepo: TypeScript Next.js apps, Python services, PostgreSQL, object storage, analytics SDKs, and third-party classroom integrations. Inventory collection, processing, retention, deletion, exports, consent, and administrator access for minors across multiple districts. Inspect logs, backups, queues, feature flags, vendor contracts as represented in code, and data-subject workflows; threat-model reidentification and account takeover without using production records. Acceptance: each data element has a system owner and lifecycle, high-risk paths have concrete evidence, deletion and export behavior is tested end to end, and remediation priorities include engineering and operational controls.

Update the content-script theme helper in the existing Manifest V3 extension to follow the website’s current `prefers-color-scheme` value. Add or remove the existing `extension-dark` class on the extension-owned overlay, and subscribe to media-query changes so the overlay updates while the page remains open. Do not alter page content, inject a second stylesheet, or add dependencies. Acceptance: light and dark initial states are correct, a system-theme change updates the class, and the listener is not registered more than once per overlay.

Stress-test and review the district analytics and reporting platform: dbt and SQL transformations on Snowflake, Airflow orchestration, Python APIs, and a React dashboard serving attendance, progress, and equity reports. Evaluate correctness across slowly changing student identities, late-arriving events, timezone boundaries, privacy suppression, and custom district definitions. Run data-quality, concurrency, backfill, and warehouse-cost experiments at five years of synthetic scale; inspect lineage, alerting, retries, and access policies. Acceptance: every executive metric has a tested definition and owner, material discrepancies are reproducible, service-level objectives and cost budgets are measured, and high-risk fixes are sequenced.

Implement a governed education data lakehouse that ingests SIS, LMS, attendance, and assessment events from hundreds of districts. Use Kafka, Debezium, Airflow, Spark, and Iceberg on cloud object storage, with schema registry, replayable raw data, quality checks, lineage, and curated research marts. Enforce tenant isolation, FERPA-aligned minimization, encryption, row-level access, deletion workflows, and pseudonymization. Acceptance requires idempotent backfills, late-event handling, contract tests, reproducible pipelines, cost monitoring, and documented recovery from a regional outage.

In the Java Spring Boot order service integrated with Stripe webhooks, fix orders being marked paid or released to fulfillment before a payment failure is processed. Make payment state transitions idempotent and allow only a verified success event to move an order from pending to paid; failed, canceled, and disputed events must stop fulfillment without overwriting a later valid success. Preserve existing retry handling. Add webhook fixtures and service tests for duplicate and out-of-order events; acceptance is no fulfillment for failed payments and consistent final status after replay.

Standardize the data-access documentation for a polyglot platform using Java/JDBC, Go/sqlc, Python/SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, and Kafka-derived read models. Cover service boundaries, read/write ownership, query conventions, schema and index design, consistency choices, transactions, caching, pagination, migrations, observability, and decommissioning. Include language-specific templates, decision records, anti-patterns, load-testing guidance, and a migration plan for legacy repositories. Acceptance: engineers can choose a store from the decision matrix, bootstrap a compliant service, and validate examples and lint rules in CI.

Build a branching dialogue system for Unity 2022 LTS in C# using Ink as the authoring format. It must support conditional choices, variables, relationship checks, quest callbacks, save/resume, localization keys, voice timing, skip/auto modes, controller navigation, and accessibility text sizing. Add an editor validation pass for unreachable nodes, missing localization, and invalid commands, while keeping narrative data separate from UI. Acceptance: writers can preview a conversation without entering gameplay, old saves migrate, choices trigger deterministic game events, localized lines render correctly, and unit/integration tests cover branching, save rollback, and missing content.

In the Rust clap upload CLI, write tests for retry and backoff decisions. Use a deterministic fake HTTP transport and injected sleeper so the suite performs no real waits or network requests. Cover a transient 503 that succeeds on the third attempt, an immediate 4xx failure with no retry, and exhaustion after the configured limit. Assert attempt count, final status, and error text. Acceptance: cargo test --offline passes and the tests prove backoff is requested only between retryable attempts.

Review the LVGL touchscreen control stack on the STM32, including input drivers, UI task scheduling, screen navigation, localization, persistent settings, the command bus, and safety interlocks for actuator controls. Check event ordering, debounce behavior, stale status display, watchdog interaction, flash wear, recovery after brownouts, and whether commands remain safe when communications fail. Evaluate separation between presentation and control logic and compatibility across the supported display variants. Acceptance requires ranked findings with evidence, an end-to-end interaction and failure matrix, proposed boundary improvements, and tests for invalid input, rapid gestures, and offline operation.

Create an end-to-end secrets detection and remediation program for the repository and delivery process. Add Gitleaks or TruffleHog pre-commit hooks, pull-request scanning, default-branch and full-history scans, artifact scanning, and GitHub push protection integration. Maintain a reviewed encrypted allowlist for unavoidable test fixtures, route confirmed findings to the security queue, automatically revoke exposed credentials where provider APIs support it, and prevent noisy checks from being bypassed. Acceptance: historical findings are triaged, new high-confidence secrets block merges and releases, false positives have an owner and expiry, leaked credentials are rotated, and dashboards show coverage, age, and remediation status.
